title: The Island
description: Ike takes Emeka across the bridge to the other Lagos: a client who needs convincing, an owambe that needs dancing, and a friend who cannot laugh.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Ike's Benz crosses Third Mainland Bridge at seven in the morning. The lagoon is silver. The traffic is not.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: Today you see the real business. Fleet managers. Big companies. They buy forty brake pads at once and nobody checks.

variants.text: And next time area boys come, you don't pay them from my till. I counted. I always count. (He doesn't sound angry. He sounds like a man writing something down.)
Ngozi told me you paid Scatter from your own pocket. (He looks at you sideways.) Stupid. Loyal. Same thing in Lagos.
The whole market says you fought Scatter. (He grins.) Now they will charge me double. Thank you, Mr Lion.
You know Professor? (A pause.) Be careful. That old man knows too much about too many people.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: Your mother is fine? Good. You still owe me thirty. I haven't forgotten. I never forget.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: When the manager asks, you say the parts are original. You are my apprentice. Your face is honest. That is your job today: your face.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A glass office. Air conditioning so cold it feels like a lie. A fleet manager in a tie with ducks on it turns a brake pad over in his hands.

beats.speaker: fleetManager
beats.text: These are original? Our drivers carry staff. Last month one of our buses lost its brakes on Ikorodu Road.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: (Ike is smiling at you. The smile has teeth.)

options.text: "Original, sir. I swear on my father's grave."
Say nothing. Let Ike do the talking.
"Sir... buy from Mama Ngozi at Ọjà. Her parts are original."

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: (in the car, very quiet) Next time, think about who brought you to Lagos before you open your mouth.

variants.text: (in the car, laughing without sound) On your father's grave! My guy. You are learning faster than I did. (He gives you ₦8,000. It is heavier than eight thousand.)

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Evening. An owambe on the Island: a chief's sixtieth birthday. Aso-ebi in gold. Two live bands fighting. Money falling like rain on the dancers.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: See that boy in the agbada? Tunde Ten-Ten. He dances at every party in Lagos and collects the money. Go and humble him. For me.

won.toast: The band leader shouts "Village boy don land!" and the whole party laughs. Everybody except one man in white.

lost.toast: Tunde Ten-Ten sprays you a ₦200 note out of pity. You keep it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: At the edge of the dance floor, a man in white watches you without blinking. Chief Ọ̀dụ̀. He raises his glass half an inch.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: After midnight, back at Ọjà. Ike parks the Benz and doesn't get out. His mother calls. He sends her ₦200,000 while she is still talking.

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: I slept on cartons too, you know. In that same shop. The rats knew me by name. (He doesn't smile.) Now look.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: He tells a story about a customer who paid with a cheque from a dead bank. It is a funny story. He tells it like a funeral announcement.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: He wants you to ask. You can feel it.

options.text: "Ike. How did you really get from the cartons to the Benz?"
"I want to get there my own way, Ike."

beats.speaker: ike
beats.text: (He starts the car again.) Not tonight. Some stories you tell, and then you can't un-tell them.

variants.text: Everything? (He looks at you a long time.) Be careful what you ask for in Lagos, Emeka. Somebody is always listening.
Your own way. (A sound that should be a laugh and isn't.) I said that too. Sleep well, Mr Own-Way.

beats.title: The Island
beats.summary: You saw the other Lagos: cold offices, gold aso-ebi, money falling like rain. You also saw a man in white raise his glass, and a friend who tells funny stories like funerals.
